title: BD FACS Aria II Start-up and Calibration
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.besajeae
materials: FACS Aria II Start Up and Calibration
BD Falcon 5 ml polystyrene round bottom tubes
Sterile falcon tissue culture 96 well plates
Single cell suspension of sample ready for sorting
BD Falcon 5 ml polystyrene round bottom tubes.
Unscrew the triangular knob all the way.
Start computer for ARIA II 478 and login.
Start BD Coherent Connection software to monitor lasers and click Start All button, and make sure that all lasers are on.
Log in to FACSDiva Software. There is no password so click OK.
Fluidics startup will run for ~10 minutes.
Install the tube onto the cytometer loading port.
Log in to the FACSDiva software as an administrator.

steps.title: Check sheath and waste tanks
steps.instruction: Inspect the sheath and waste tanks and fill them if necessary.

steps.title: Depressurize and open tank lid
steps.instruction: Pull up the pressure release ring to depressurize the tank, then push down on the lid until it releases, rotate the lid to the side, lift the retaining bracket, and remove the entire lid assembly.

steps.title: Fill sheath and empty waste tanks
steps.instruction: Fill the sheath tank to the upper tank weld with BD Sheath Fluid; empty the waste tank into the sink, reinstall it, and cover the bottom of the tank with bleach.

steps.title: Power on instrument and launch software
steps.instruction: Turn the Aria on by pressing the big green button and wait until the Tera Term program opens; when Tera Term opens, Vx Works will appear on the computer screen.

steps.title: Perform Fluidic Startup
steps.instruction: In BD FACSDiva select Cytometer > Fluidic Startup and complete the prompted actions:

substeps.instruction: Verify that air and fluid lines are disconnected from the ethanol tank and connected to the sheath tank; click Done.
Verify that a closed‑loop nozzle is installed in the flow cell; click Done.

When prompted, remove the closed‑loop nozzle: rotate the black knob below the nozzle counter‑clockwise to 7 o’clock, gently pull out the nozzle, and store it in the gray nozzle holder to the right of the flow cell.
Insert the correct nozzle (typically 130 µm); rotate the black knob clockwise to 12 o’clock to secure; click Done.
When Fluidic Startup is complete, turn on the stream by clicking the Stream button in the Break‑off window.

steps.title: Warm up lasers and fluidics
steps.instruction: Allow at least 30 minutes for the lasers to warm up and the fluidics to stabilize.

steps.title: Adjust laser amplitude and fluidics
steps.instruction: After stabilization, adjust the amplitude slider so the break‑off point is near the middle of the Break‑off window and the Gap reading is 12; ensure at least three distinct drops are visible, satellite drops merge with the main drops, and the stream is centered in the window.

steps.title: Optional: Activate cooling bath
steps.instruction: If sorting into cooled tubes, turn on the Lauda cooling bath during the warm‑up and stabilization step.

steps.title: Optional: Activate aerosol abatement
steps.instruction: Turn on the Aerosol Abatement Device and set the air‑flow rate to 20 % to prevent release of harmful aerosols.

steps.title: Prepare CS&T bead dilution
steps.instruction: In a 5 mL tube dilute 1 drop of CS&T beads into 500 µL of 1× PBS; store the dilution at 4 °C in the dark for up to 5 days.

steps.title: Run CS&T calibration (CST)
steps.instruction: Open Cytometer > CST (a separate program from Diva); verify that the bead lot information under Setup > BEADS matches the Cytometer Setup and Tracking bead lot.

steps.title: Check CS&T performance
steps.instruction: In the Setup Control window select Check Performance from the Characterize menu and click Run; the performance check takes about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Interpret CS&T results
steps.instruction: When CS&T performance completes, note the result (Pass, Pass with warnings, or Fail). If Fail or Pass with warnings, view the report to assess impact on the experiment. If the bead lot information does not match, update the bead lot as follows:

substeps.instruction: Click Cytometer > CST > Tools > Bead Lots, select the appropriate bead lot, and click OK.
Download the bead‑lot file to a workstation and save it.
Return to the CST Tool window, open the Bead Lots dialog, click Import, select the .bls file, and click Open.

steps.title: Define baseline with CST beads
steps.instruction: Install the tube containing CST beads onto the cytometer loading port and click Run; allow approximately 30 minutes (prepare ~2 mL of bead suspension). When baseline definition completes, note the Pass/Warning/Fail result and act as above if needed.

steps.title: Set up stream parameters
steps.instruction: Ensure the nozzle/sheath pressure is appropriate for the current nozzle, then establish a stable drop pattern:

substeps.instruction: Allow at least 30 minutes for lasers to warm up and fluidics to stabilize (if not already done).
Adjust the amplitude slider until the drop break‑off is approximately in the top third of the Break‑off window.
Do not adjust the nozzle‑oscillation frequency; it varies with nozzle size and should generally remain unchanged.
For a 130 µm nozzle, set the Gap value to 12 (different nozzles require different Gaps).
Set the Drop 1 value according to the guideline that places the break‑off near the top third of the window (see user guide table).
Keep the Amplitude value ≤ 70; if > 70 is required, ensure the Attenuation option is OFF. If the Amplitude must be < ≈ 8 and fine‑tuning the Gap is difficult, turn ON Attenuation.

steps.title: Enable Sweet Spot function
steps.instruction: When the drop pattern is stable, turn on the Sweet Spot; it will automatically adjust amplitude to maintain the stream at the target values you have set.

steps.title: Configure Aerosol Management System (AMS)
steps.instruction: If using the AMS, keep all doors closed and perform the following:

substeps.instruction: Ensure the main POWER button on the back of the evacuator is ON.
Press the POWER button on the evacuator’s membrane panel.
Set the suction control rate to 20 % (do not exceed 20 % as higher rates may affect side‑stream stability).
Verify that the filter flow gauge reads less than 2.4 inches.

steps.title: Clog remediation procedure
steps.instruction: If a clog is encountered, execute these steps:

substeps.instruction: Turn the stream OFF while keeping the top and flow‑chamber doors CLOSED.
Turn the suction rate up to 100 % and allow at least 1 minute to evacuate aerosols from the sort chamber.
Remove the nozzle and clean it: place the nozzle in a clean FACS tube with Milli‑Q H₂O, cap the tube, sonicate for 1 minute, then remove the nozzle and dry with Kimwipes.
Put the AMS on standby by pressing the POWER button on the membrane panel when sorting is finished.
